name: AI Signals in the DAX 40
description: This report benchmarks the 40 constituents of the DAX on the basis of publicly observable signals of organisational AI readiness. Using a transparent 15-criterion framework across five dimensions – strategy and leadership, adoption and scaling, data/technology/ecosystem, governance and responsible AI, and organisation and talent – each company was scored on a 0–3 anchored scale from official corporate sources (annual reports, investor materials, corporate websites, press releases and published AI policies) published between 1 January 2025 and the cut-off date of 15 September 2026. The benchmark rests on 600 criterion-level evidence entries drawn from 150 distinct documents, all of which are documented in the accompanying evidence log. The mean total score across the index is 1.81 on the 0–3 scale (index value 60/100) with a wide spread (standard deviation 0.69; range 0.27–2.93). Adoption signals are the most widely disclosed dimension (mean 2.30), while governance and responsible-AI signals are the least widely disclosed and most dispersed (mean 1.39, SD 0.98); in 75% of companies adoption signals exceed governance signals. Only about one in five companies publishes a quantified AI target system, and only one company reports an external AI management-system certification.
